zh.title: 初高中英语提分，为什么要先音标、再词汇、再语法刷题？
zh.description: AI脑波英语解释初高中英语提分路径：先修复音标和自然拼读，再集中突破词汇，然后用语法、听力、阅读、写作和刷卷复盘转化成考试分数。
zh.lead: 很多学生英语提不上去，不是单点问题，而是音标、词汇、语法、听读写和刷卷复盘没有形成顺序。

sections.h2: 为什么不能一上来就刷卷子？
paragraphs: 如果孩子单词读不准、词汇量不足、句子结构看不懂，刷卷只会暴露问题，很难真正解决问题。
AI脑波英语会先测基础，再判断该从音标、词汇、语法还是题型专项切入。对基础薄弱的学生来说，顺序比努力更重要。

sections.h2: 为什么要先修复音标和自然拼读？
paragraphs: 很多孩子背单词慢，不是记忆力差，而是不会读、读不准、音形义没有连接起来。
音标和自然拼读打牢后，孩子看到新词更容易读出来，听到单词更容易辨出来，背词也不再完全靠死记硬背。

sections.h2: 为什么词汇是核心突破口？
paragraphs: 词汇一旦稳住，会直接帮助听力、阅读、完形和写作。很多孩子听不懂、读不懂、写不出，本质上都和词汇底座不稳有关。
AI脑波英语学习舱适合做词汇的节律化输入、出舱检测和复现巩固，但训练不能停留在“听过了”，必须当场测、隔天复现。

sections.h2: 词汇之后，语法、听力、阅读、写作怎么接上？
paragraphs: 词汇突破以后，还要补语法结构。孩子要能看懂主谓宾、时态、从句和长难句，否则阅读和写作仍然会卡住。
听力要训练场景词、关键词定位和听音辨词；阅读和完形要做长难句、题型方法和限时训练；写作要做句型、连接词、结构和批改重写。

sections.h2: 刷卷子应该放在什么时候？
paragraphs: 刷卷不是越早越好，也不是越多越好。基础没稳就刷整卷，孩子容易越刷越挫败。
更合理的方式是先专项后整卷，先不限时找问题，再限时练速度。每次刷卷都要做错题归因：到底是词汇不会、语法不懂、审题错误、时间不够，还是题型方法不熟。

faqs.q: 英语提分一定要先学音标吗？
faqs.a: 如果孩子读词不准、拼读困难，建议先修复音标或自然拼读，否则背词效率会很低。
学习舱主要用于词汇输入、听辨和复现，但考试提分还需要语法、听力、阅读、写作和刷卷复盘。
基础词汇和语法有一定稳定度后再逐步刷专项卷和整卷，刷完必须复盘错因。

faqs.q: 家长怎么判断孩子适合哪条路径？
faqs.a: 先做入学测评，看音标、词汇、语法、听读写和试卷失分点，再确定训练顺序和目标。

zh.cta: 如果孩子英语长期卡住，建议先做入学测评，判断音标、词汇、语法和题型短板，再制定训练方案。

en.title: Why English improvement should start with phonics, vocabulary, grammar and then exam practice
en.description: AI Brainwave English explains a practical improvement path for middle and high school students: phonics, vocabulary, grammar, listening, reading, writing and exam-paper review.
en.lead: Many students do not improve because the learning order is broken: pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, listening, reading, writing and paper review need to work together.

sections.h2: Why not start with endless exam papers?
paragraphs: If a student cannot pronounce words, recognize vocabulary or understand sentence structure, more papers may expose the problem without fixing it.
A better path starts with assessment and then trains the missing foundation first.

sections.h2: Why phonics and pronunciation come first
paragraphs: Many students struggle with vocabulary because sound, spelling and meaning are not connected.
When phonics and pronunciation improve, students can read new words more confidently, recognize words by sound and reduce the pressure of memorizing everything mechanically.

sections.h2: Why vocabulary is the main breakthrough
paragraphs: Stable vocabulary supports listening, reading, cloze tasks and writing. Many listening and reading problems are actually vocabulary problems first.
The learning cabin is used for rhythmic input, exit testing and review, but every session must include testing and follow-up review.

sections.h2: How grammar, listening, reading and writing connect
paragraphs: After vocabulary improves, students still need grammar structure. Sentence patterns, tense, clauses and long-sentence analysis help reading and writing.
Listening needs scene words and keyword tracking. Reading and cloze need long-sentence work and question-type methods. Writing needs sentence patterns, linking words, correction and rewriting.
Paper practice should not be random. Students should move from targeted exercises to full papers, and from untimed diagnosis to timed practice.
Every wrong answer should be classified: vocabulary, phrase, grammar, sentence structure, listening keyword, careless mistake, time pressure or method problem.

faqs.q: Should students learn phonics before vocabulary?
faqs.a: If pronunciation and spelling are weak, phonics should be repaired first because it improves vocabulary efficiency.

faqs.q: Does the learning cabin solve every English problem?
faqs.a: No. It supports vocabulary input and review, but exam improvement also needs grammar, listening, reading, writing and paper practice.

faqs.q: When should students start exam papers?
faqs.a: After the key foundation is more stable, students can move into targeted papers and full timed practice with error analysis.

faqs.q: How should a family choose the right path?
faqs.a: Start with an assessment of phonics, vocabulary, grammar, listening, reading, writing and exam gaps.

en.cta: Start with an assessment to understand whether the student is blocked by phonics, vocabulary, grammar or exam skills.
